card.intuition: A model provider request is one round-trip from the harness to the provider: the harness sends the current context and the provider returns one response — a tool call or a final answer. A single user turn can spawn many requests because each tool result triggers another. Requests, not turns, are the unit of billing.
card.analogy: Each request is a fresh drive-thru order: no matter how many you've placed before, you hand over your full order list every time, and the kitchen keeps nothing between visits.
card.time_complexity: Cost is proportional to the number of requests times the size of the context each one carries — an innocuous question can cost more than your message because forty turns of history re-send on every request.
card.space_complexity: Each request re-sends the whole session — system prompt, conversation, tool results — so the context window is re-occupied every round-trip; the prefix cache is what makes the repetition affordable.
when_to_use: Explaining where the tokens went: count the requests, not the turns
Predicting bill spikes from tool-heavy turns — twelve greps, eight reads, four edits
Reasoning about dual billing of input plus output on every request
gotchas: A turn is not a request — one 'fix the failing test' plays out as a chain of six requests
The provider keeps nothing between requests; request forty resends what thirty-nine sent plus one tool result

steps.label: User turn
steps.annotation: You give a single instruction such as fix the failing test.

steps.label: Request 1
steps.annotation: The harness sends context; the model returns a tool call to run the tests.

steps.label: Harness acts
steps.annotation: Tests run and the output is appended to the context.

steps.label: Requests 2-5
steps.annotation: Each new request re-sends the whole growing context.

steps.label: Final answer
steps.annotation: The chain ends with a final answer; every request is billed separately.

exercise.prompt: Count how many model provider requests a turn will spawn: one for the original instruction, plus one for every tool result that must be fed back in.
hints: Start with the single request that started the turn
Each tool result in the list triggers exactly one follow-up request
